description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs lines 16-38 (the crate-level Quick start doc) shows verify_chain with six arguments including '&NoAiaFetcher' but the comment next to the last arg is:

    &NoAiaFetcher,      // or an  from 

That is misleading on two axes:

1. A new reader has no way to tell from this snippet whether NoAiaFetcher is 'the default for offline use' or 'something I should replace.' The Quick start is the first thing users read. They will copy NoAiaFetcher and never look at it again.

2. The cross-reference points at pkix-aia-http but the snippet doesn't say WHEN to use it. The user has to read the Limitations section (line 73) to find out that the use-case wrappers (verify_tls_server, etc.) bake NoAiaFetcher internally and that 'callers that want AIA fetching must drop down to verify_chain or construct a Verifier directly.'

SUGGESTED REWRITE: add a one-line decision rule next to the NoAiaFetcher in the snippet:

    &NoAiaFetcher,      // use  from  if the
                        // caller-supplied chain may be missing intermediates

…and split the Quick start into 'common case: complete chain' and 'with AIA fetching: incomplete chain' subsections, mirroring the README's structure. The Quick start currently has one example (Reusable verifier) that ALSO uses new_no_aia (line 56) — so a reader learns two ways to disable AIA before being told what AIA is.

Alternatively, drop the Quick start use of '&NoAiaFetcher' entirely and show '&HttpFetcher::new()' from pkix-aia-http (gated behind a feature). The default should communicate the recommended path, not the do-nothing path.

The CHANGELOG entry for PKIX-zkjb.7 ('AIA chain reassembly') describes the feature in detail but the user-facing Quick start gives no indication that AIA exists or matters.
title: Quick-start docstring uses NoAiaFetcher with 6-arg verify_chain but doesnt explain why or when to opt into AIA
